text:
chris: Heads-up — rolling a small agent that snapshot-collects dmesg + journalctl + periodic `nvidia-smi -q` at drain time (and on Xid/ECC events). Goal: stitch traces across reboots so we can attribute flaky cards faster. PTAL on the plan below.

maria: Nice. Do we compress on-node or stream? also: privacy scrub?

chris: Compress on-node (xz) then upload to internal S3 path with node id. We scrub PII and kernel printk payloads >8k. Only keep kernel OOPS headers + surrounding 1k lines.

ben: Quick sketch of the collector (pseudocode):
```bash
# run during drain or when NVML reports Xid
mkdir -p /var/tmp/gpu_snapshots/$NODEID
journalctl -k -b -1 --no-pager > $DIR/journal_previous_boot.log || true
dmesg --ctime --level=err,warn > $DIR/dmesg_errors.log || true
nvidia-smi -q -a > $DIR/nvidia_smi_full.log || true
# include driver, gpu UUID, busid
echo "driver: $(modinfo nvidia | grep version)" > $DIR/driver_meta.txt
# pack and upload
tar -cJf $ARCHIVE -C $DIR . && aws s3 cp $ARCHIVE s3://redwood-gpu-snaps/$NODEID/$ARCHIVE --acl private
```

dave: Two parsing tips from past Xid hairballs:
- capture `Xid` numeric values and map to NV driver doc ranges (e.g., 13=ECC/clock/thermal-ish, 46=nvlink/firmware).
- correlate `nvidia-smi -q` memory ECC counts with `dmesg` lines that contain `EDAC`/`ecc` to decide hardware vs SW.

maria: Would like a unique sequence id added to each snapshot so downstream parsers can stitch across upload retries. Also include `container_pid` if drain triggered by pod OOMs.

chris: Good call. We'll add header file `snapshot_meta.json` with: node_id, snapshot_id, epoch_ts, kernel_version, driver_version, gpu_busid, gpu_uuid, attached_pods (list), trigger_reason (drain|xid|manual). We'll keep it small (meta only).

ben: One more: include a tiny `nvml-log.txt` that records time-series of temperature/mem/error counters sampled every 5s for 60s before drain. That often shows trend before a hard Xid.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolling out gpu-snapshotter v0.3 to canary pool (10 nodes) at 1768543225. Monitor /s3 prefix `s3://redwood-gpu-snaps/canary/` for new objects.

maria: Throttling note — don't upload >10MB per node by default. If archive >10MB, gzip and only keep top error groups + `nvidia_smi_full.log` truncated to last 200 lines. We hit cost spike last time.

chris: We'll implement size cap and an opt-in full dump flag for oncall. Also auto-delete local snapshots after successful upload.

dave: Parsing heuristics I'll add to the triage playbook:
- regex: `Xid\s*(\d+)` -> xid_code
- capture `GPU UUID|PCI Bus|Serial` from `nvidia-smi -q`
- check `journalctl -k` for `EDAC`/`IOMMU`/`GPU` within +-5s window of Xid timestamp
- if ECC corrected >0 and uncorrected==0 => probable soft ECC event; if uncorrected>0 -> immediate drain/replace flag

maria: How do we surface these snapshots in the console? Link from node page to last 3 snapshots?

chris: Yes: console will show last 3 snapshots with parsed highlights (xid summary, driver, serial, candidate cause). Link goes to S3 object (internal). We'll only show parsed highlights by default to avoid huge downloads.

ben: For oncall workflows, add `--collect-on-xid` boolean to the agent so it can run outside of drain (some flakies never get drained before failure).

chris: Plan for rollout: canary (10), staging (50), then prod. We'll re-run canary after 24h and check false positives.

maria: LGTM. If infra-bot sees >3 distinct nodes with same serial failing within 72h, auto-create a hardware ticket in ops queue.

infra-bot: infra-bot: created ticket #HW-1324 (auto) for serial SN-REPEATED-001 after 4 fails in 48h.

dave: One more ops rule: if `uncorrected_ecc > 0` in any snapshot, prefer immediate node drain + hardware escalate, and annotate node w/ `gpu:suspect-uncorrected` tag.

chris: Thanks all. I'll push the PR for the collector and add the parsing rules to the triage doc. If you want access to snapshot S3 path to test parsers ping me. :rocket:
